analysis:
MARKET & REGIME: SPY is in a MIXED regime — price sits 1.4% below its SMA50 while the 20-day slope has ticked back to barely positive (+0.60%). This is an indeterminate environment that rewards patience over activity. Forcing entries here risks adding to an already stretched book.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW: We are at maximum concentration — 5 positions, 74% deployed, against a stated 3-5 position cap. There is no structural capacity to add a 6th name without violating the concentration discipline. Each existing position deserves individual scrutiny:

• ULTA (+6.79%): The clear winner. Thesis intact, let it run. No action needed.
• UHS (-0.63%) and FOXA (-0.67%): Essentially flat. No thesis break signals visible. Hold and monitor.
• ADSK (-2.01%): Small unrealized loss, well within tolerable range. No action.
• AMP (-8.47%, $547.12 → $500.80): This is the most pressing concern. Ameriprise has shed 8.47% from entry — approaching a level where original stop logic should be reviewed. If the original stop was set at 1.5-2x ATR below entry (~10-12%), we may be approaching or past it. In a mixed-to-soft market for financial services, AMP's setup is deteriorating. The position should be watched very closely; if price fails to reclaim the $510-515 zone and the thesis (earnings power, buybacks, financial sector re-rating) no longer supports holding, a discretionary exit is warranted even without a hard stop being triggered mechanically. Flag for possible manual exit on next leg down.

CANDIDATE SCREEN: Several quality names passed the filter with genuine merit — TEL (TE Connectivity) stands out with fwd P/E 14, PEG 1.23, +5.3% EPS revision, near-SMA50 in the lower 36% of its 52-week range, and no near-term earnings risk (79 days out). NXPI (NXP Semiconductors) offers PEG 0.52 and strong fundamentals but is already +11.6% vs SMA50, slightly extended. ORLY (O'Reilly) is a basing setup in the lower 28% of range but lacks confirmed uptrend (SMA50 slope -1.3%). None of these can be initiated today without exceeding the 5-position hard cap.

DECISION: Zero new trades. The correct action is to hold existing positions, manage AMP risk carefully, let ULTA run, and preserve the 26% cash buffer. Forcing a 6th position in a MIXED regime against a 5-position cap would be a process violation, not a value-add. Cash at ~26% is the right posture until either (a) AMP exits, creating redeployment capacity, or (b) market regime clarifies into a confirmed uptrend. The Sortino ratio of -12.81 is a red flag demanding that the next entry, when it comes, is genuinely high-conviction and well-timed — not forced by activity bias.
